```{r setup, echo=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 12,
  fig.height = 4.5
)

# shared settings and helpers (defined once, used throughout)
alpha <- 0.05                                    # significance level

fmt_p <- function(p) if_else(is.na(p), NA_character_,
                             if_else(p < 0.0001, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p, 3))))

hc3 <- function(m) vcovHC(m, type = "HC3")       # heteroskedasticity-robust covariance
nw  <- function(m, ...) NeweyWest(m, prewhite = FALSE, ...)   # HAC covariance
```

```{r date_setup}
start_date <- ymd("2017-12-01")
end_date   <- ymd("2025-12-31")
```

```{r load fred}
invisible(getSymbols(c("DCOILWTICO", "SP500", "VIXCLS"), src = "FRED", auto.assign = TRUE))

us_daily <- merge(DCOILWTICO, SP500, VIXCLS)
us_daily <- us_daily[paste0(start_date, "/", end_date)]

df_us_daily <- tibble(
  date  = as.Date(index(us_daily)),
  WTI   = as.numeric(us_daily$DCOILWTICO),
  SP500 = as.numeric(us_daily$SP500),
  VIX   = as.numeric(us_daily$VIXCLS)
)
```

```{r load lseg-ph-finmkt}
# convert excel date to real date
excel_date <- function(x) as.Date(as.numeric(x), origin = "1899-12-30")

# 10y bond yield data starts at 19th row, 12/17-12/25
ph_10y_raw <- read_excel("PH_10Y_GS_YIELD_1825.xlsx", skip = 18)
ph_10y_daily <- ph_10y_raw |>
  select(date = Date, PH_10Y_GS_Yield = `Yield to Maturity`) |>
  mutate(
    date = excel_date(date),
    PH_10Y_GS_Yield = as.numeric(PH_10Y_GS_Yield)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(date) & between(date, start_date, end_date))

# PSEI data starts at 33rd row, 12/17-12/25
psei_raw <- read_excel("PSEI_1825.xlsx", skip = 32)
psei_daily <- psei_raw |>
  select(date = `Exchange Date`, PSEI = Close) |>
  mutate(
    date = excel_date(date),
    PSEI =as.numeric(PSEI)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(date) & between(date, start_date, end_date))

# USD/PHP starts at 29th row, 12/17-12/25
usdphp_raw <- read_excel("USDPHP_1825.xlsx", skip = 28)
usdphp_daily <- usdphp_raw |>
  select(date = `Exchange Date`, USD_PHP = `Mid Price`) |>
  mutate(
    date = excel_date(date),
    USD_PHP =as.numeric(USD_PHP)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(date) & between(date, start_date, end_date))

# Parsed RRP starts at 3rd row. Parsing c/o from RRP text using Claude Sonnet 5.5
rrp_raw <- read_excel("PH_RRP_1725.xlsx", skip = 2,                       col_names = c("date", "BSP_RRP_Rate"))

rrp_1725 <- rrp_raw |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    BSP_RRP_Rate = as.numeric(BSP_RRP_Rate)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(date) & date <= end_date) |>
  arrange(date)
```

```{r load lseg-ph-macroecon}
read_ph_macro <- function(filepath, var_name) {
  read_excel(filepath, skip = 1, col_names = c("date", var_name)) |>
    mutate(
      # Truncate to first of the month for easier/cleaner relational joins
      year_month = floor_date(as.Date(date), "month"),
      across(all_of(var_name), as.numeric)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(year_month), if_all(all_of(var_name), \(x) !is.na(x))) |>
    select(year_month, all_of(var_name))
}

cpi_monthly  <- read_ph_macro("PH_CPI_YY_1626.xlsx", "PH_CPI")
m3_monthly   <- read_ph_macro("PH_M3_YY_1626.xlsx", "PH_M3")
mfg_monthly  <- read_ph_macro("PH_Manufacturing_Production_YY_1626.xlsx", "PH_Manufacturing_Production")
```

```{r consolidate main-dataframe}
daily_financials <- psei_daily |>
  full_join(usdphp_daily, by = "date") |>
  full_join(ph_10y_daily, by = "date") |>
  full_join(df_us_daily, by = "date") |>
  arrange(date) |>
  # forward fill missing based on last previous day/data
  tidyr::fill(PSEI, USD_PHP, PH_10Y_GS_Yield, WTI, SP500, .direction = "down")

# month-end value; NA (not size 0) when a month has no observations yet
last_valid <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x[length(x)]
}

financial_monthly <- daily_financials |>
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(date, unit = "month")) |>
  group_by(year_month) |>
  summarise(
    PSEI            = last_valid(PSEI),
    USD_PHP         = last_valid(USD_PHP),
    PH_10Y_GS_Yield = last_valid(PH_10Y_GS_Yield),
    WTI             = last_valid(WTI),
    SP500           = last_valid(SP500),
    VIX             = if (all(is.na(VIX))) NA_real_ else mean(VIX, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups         = "drop"
  )

# one row per month, Dec 2017 - Dec 2025
month_spine <- tibble(
  year_month = seq(floor_date(start_date, "month"),
                   floor_date(end_date, "month"), by = "month")
)

# BSP RRP rate in force at each month-end (rate changes on meeting dates)
rrp_monthly <- month_spine |>
  mutate(
    month_end    = ceiling_date(year_month, "month") - days(1),
    rrp_idx      = findInterval(as.numeric(month_end), 
                                as.numeric(rrp_1725$date)),
    BSP_RRP_Rate = if_else(rrp_idx == 0, NA_real_,
                           rrp_1725$BSP_RRP_Rate[pmax(rrp_idx, 1)])
  ) |>
  select(year_month, BSP_RRP_Rate)

df_econometrics <- month_spine |>
  left_join(financial_monthly, by = "year_month") |>
  left_join(rrp_monthly,       by = "year_month") |>
  left_join(cpi_monthly,       by = "year_month") |>
  left_join(m3_monthly,        by = "year_month") |>
  left_join(mfg_monthly,       by = "year_month") |>
  arrange(year_month) |>
  mutate(
    # monthly log returns / log changes (month-end levels)
    PSEI    = log(PSEI)    - log(lag(PSEI)),
    SP500   = log(SP500)   - log(lag(SP500)),
    USD_PHP = log(USD_PHP) - log(lag(USD_PHP)),
    WTI     = log(WTI)     - log(lag(WTI)),
    # month-end first differences
    BSP_RRP_Rate    = BSP_RRP_Rate    - lag(BSP_RRP_Rate),
    PH_10Y_GS_Yield = PH_10Y_GS_Yield - lag(PH_10Y_GS_Yield)
    # PH_CPI, PH_M3, PH_Manufacturing_Production are already YoY %
  ) |>
  # drop 2017 since only 2018-2025
  filter(year(year_month) >= 2018)

glimpse(df_econometrics)
head(df_econometrics)
```

```{r data-quality-checks}
# check for structure: row count, month coverage, duplicates, gaps
expected_months <- seq(ymd("2018-01-01"), ymd("2025-12-01"), by = "month")
tibble(
  rows               = nrow(df_econometrics),
  expected_rows      = length(expected_months),
  first_month        = min(df_econometrics$year_month),
  last_month         = max(df_econometrics$year_month),
  duplicate_months   = sum(duplicated(df_econometrics$year_month)),
  missing_months     = sum(!expected_months %in% df_econometrics$year_month),
  is_sorted          = !is.unsorted(df_econometrics$year_month)
) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "check", values_to = "value",
               values_transform = as.character) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Structure and month coverage")

# identify data types, missing, non-finite, constant columns
df_econometrics |>
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    type     = ~ class(.x)[1],
    n_na     = ~ sum(is.na(.x)),
    pct_na   = ~ round(100 * mean(is.na(.x)), 1),
    n_inf    = ~ sum(is.infinite(.x)),
    n_unique = ~ n_distinct(.x)
  ), .names = "{.col}__{.fn}")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
               names_sep = "__") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Data types, missing observations and non-finite values")

# identify months with missing values
df_econometrics |>
  filter(if_any(-year_month, is.na)) |>
  transmute(year_month, missing_vars = pmap_chr(pick(-year_month),
              function(...) paste(names(c(...))[is.na(c(...))], collapse = ", "))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Months with missing values")
```

```{r descriptive-stats}
# math functions
skewness <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^1.5
excess_kurtosis <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^2 - 3
n_outliers <- function(x, z = 3) sum(abs(x - mean(x)) / sd(x) > z)

vars <- setdiff(names(df_econometrics), "year_month")

num_long <- df_econometrics |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = vars))

desc_stats <- num_long |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    mean        = mean(value),
    median      = median(value),
    min         = min(value),
    max         = max(value),
    range       = max - min,
    sd          = sd(value),
    skewness    = skewness(value),
    ex_kurtosis = excess_kurtosis(value),
    n_outliers  = n_outliers(value),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

desc_stats |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Descriptive statistics (excess kurtosis; normal = 0; outliers = |z| > 3)")

# plausibility definitions
tibble(
  check = c("VIX <= 0", "PH_CPI outside [-5, 25]%", "PH_M3 outside [-20, 40]%",
            "PH_Manufacturing_Production outside [-50, 100]%",
            "|monthly log return| > 0.25 (PSEI, SP500, USD_PHP, WTI)"),
  n_flagged = c(
    sum(df_econometrics$VIX <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(!between(df_econometrics$PH_CPI, -5, 25), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(!between(df_econometrics$PH_M3, -20, 40), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(!between(df_econometrics$PH_Manufacturing_Production, -50, 100), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(abs(as.matrix(df_econometrics[c("PSEI", "SP500", "USD_PHP", "WTI")])) > 0.25,
        na.rm = TRUE)
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Plausibility checks")

# panel labels carrying the statistics
panel_labels <- desc_stats |>
  transmute(
    variable,
    lab_center = sprintf("%s\nmean = %.3f | median = %.3f", variable, mean, median),
    lab_spread = sprintf("%s\nrange = %.3f | sd = %.3f", variable, range, sd),
    lab_shape  = sprintf("%s\nskew = %.2f | ex. kurtosis = %.2f", variable, skewness, ex_kurtosis)
  ) |>
  
  mutate(across(starts_with("lab_"), ~ factor(.x, levels = .x)))

plot_data <- num_long |> left_join(panel_labels, by = "variable")
stat_lines <- desc_stats |>
  select(variable, mean, median) |>
  pivot_longer(c(mean, median), names_to = "stat", values_to = "x") |>
  left_join(panel_labels, by = "variable")
```

```{r correlation-matrix, fig.height=8}
# pairwise-complete Pearson correlations
cor_matrix <- df_econometrics |>
  select(all_of(vars)) |>
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

round(cor_matrix, 3) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pearson correlation matrix")

# correlation heatmaps: all coefficients, then with the significance rule applied
cor_pvalues <- outer(vars, vars, Vectorize(function(a, b) {
  if (a == b) return(0)
  cor.test(df_econometrics[[a]], df_econometrics[[b]])$p.value
}))
dimnames(cor_pvalues) <- dimnames(cor_matrix)

# version 1: all correlations shown
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", order = "original",
         addCoef.col = "black", number.cex = 0.7, tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45,
         diag = FALSE, mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
         title = "Correlation matrix (all pairs)")

# version 2: with blank cells if not significant at the 5% level

         addCoef.col = "black", number.cex = 0.7, tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45,
         p.mat = cor_pvalues, sig.level = 0.05, insig = "blank",
         diag = FALSE, mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
         title = "Correlation matrix (blank = not significant at 5%)")

  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "r") |>
  filter(match(var1, vars) < match(var2, vars)) |>

cor_pairs |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(r = round(r, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ten strongest pairwise correlations")
```

```{r initial-mlr}
# Initial model: MLR Model: PSEI_t = b0 + b1 SP500_t + b2 USD_PHP_t + b3 BSP_RRP_Rate_t + b4 PH_10Y_GS_Yield_t + b5 PH_CPI_t + b6 PH_M3_t + b7 PH_Manufacturing_Production_t + b8 WTI_t + b9 VIX_t + e_t

regressors <- setdiff(vars, "PSEI")
mlr_formula <- reformulate(regressors, response = "PSEI")
mlr_formula

# complete-case estimation sample (January 2018 drops out: no base month for the
# returns / differences). Every model in the report is fitted on these rows.
df_model <- df_econometrics |>
  select(year_month, PSEI, all_of(regressors)) |>
  drop_na()
n_obs <- nrow(df_model)

# lm() linear model generator
model_initial <- lm(mlr_formula, data = df_model)

# coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, 95% confidence intervals
tidy(model_initial, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) |>
  transmute(
    term,
    estimate,
    std_error = std.error,
    t_stat    = statistic,
    p_value   = if_else(p.value < 0.0001, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p.value,     3))),
    ci_lower  = conf.low,
    ci_upper  = conf.high,
    signif    = case_when(p.value < 0.01 ~ "***", p.value < 0.05 ~ "**",
                          p.value < 0.10 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Initial MLR: PSEI on 9 regressors (OLS)")

# R-squared, adjusted R-squared and the overall F-test
model_fstat <- summary(model_initial)$fstatistic

glance(model_initial) |>
  transmute(
    n                = nobs,
    r_squared        = r.squared,
    adj_r_squared    = adj.r.squared,
    residual_std_err = sigma,
    f_statistic      = statistic,
    f_df_numerator   = model_fstat[["numdf"]],
    f_df_denominator = model_fstat[["dendf"]],
    f_p_value        = if_else(p.value < 0.0001, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p.value, 3)))
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value",
               values_transform = as.character) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model fit and overall F-test (H0: all slope coefficients = 0)")
```

```{r coefficient-tests}
# Individual t-tests on each slope of model_initial.
df_res <- df.residual(model_initial)
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df_res)

# Significance: H0: beta_j = 0 vs H1: beta_j != 0 (two-sided).
# Rejecting H0 <=> p < alpha <=> the (1 - alpha) CI excludes 0.
coef_tests <- tidy(model_initial) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    H0       = paste0("b(", term, ") = 0"),
    H1       = paste0("b(", term, ") != 0"),
    decision = if_else(p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0")
  )

coef_tests |>
  transmute(
    H0, H1,
    estimate,
    std_error = std.error,
    t_stat    = statistic,
    df        = df_res,
    t_crit    = t_crit,
    p_value   = if_else(p.value < 0.0001, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p.value, 3))),
    decision
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "(A) Two-sided t-tests, alpha = 0.05")

# Directional tests where theory gives an expected sign (one-sided, alpha = 0.05).
# WTI is left two-sided only: the sign is ambiguous for a net oil importer whose
# equities also co-move with risk appetite.
expected_sign <- tribble(
  ~term,                         ~sign, ~rationale,
  "SP500",                       "+",   "global equity co-movement",
  "USD_PHP",                     "-",   "peso depreciation -> foreign outflows",
  "BSP_RRP_Rate",                "-",   "policy tightening raises discount rates",
  "PH_10Y_GS_Yield",             "-",   "higher yields lower equity valuations",
  "PH_CPI",                      "-",   "inflation erodes real earnings",
  "PH_M3",                       "+",   "more liquidity supports prices",
  "PH_Manufacturing_Production", "+",   "stronger real activity",
  "VIX",                         "-",   "risk aversion"
)

coef_tests |>
  inner_join(expected_sign, by = "term") |>
  mutate(
    H0 = paste0("b(", term, ") ", if_else(sign == "+", "<= 0", ">= 0")),
    H1 = paste0("b(", term, ") ", if_else(sign == "+", "> 0", "< 0")),
    # one-sided p-value: half the two-sided p if the estimate has the expected sign
    p_one = if_else(sign(estimate) == if_else(sign == "+", 1, -1), p.value / 2, 1 - p.value / 2),
    t_crit_one = if_else(sign == "+", qt(1 - alpha, df_res), qt(alpha, df_res)),
    decision = if_else(p_one < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    H0, H1, rationale,
    estimate,
    t_stat     = statistic,
    t_crit     = t_crit_one,
    p_one_sided = if_else(p_one < 0.0001, "<0.0001", as.character(signif(p_one, 3))),
    decision
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "(B) One-sided tests against the theoretically expected sign")

# (C) Parameter uncertainty: confidence intervals at three levels.
ci_90 <- confint(model_initial, level = 0.90)
ci_95 <- confint(model_initial, level = 0.95)
ci_99 <- confint(model_initial, level = 0.99)

slopes <- coef_tests$term
tibble(
  term       = slopes,
  estimate   = coef_tests$estimate,
  `90% low`  = ci_90[slopes, 1], `90% high` = ci_90[slopes, 2],
  `95% low`  = ci_95[slopes, 1], `95% high` = ci_95[slopes, 2],
  `99% low`  = ci_99[slopes, 1], `99% high` = ci_99[slopes, 2],
  `95% width` = ci_95[slopes, 2] - ci_95[slopes, 1],
  `0 in 95% CI?` = if_else(ci_95[slopes, 1] <= 0 & ci_95[slopes, 2] >= 0,
                           "Yes (not significant)", "No (significant)")
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "(C) Confidence intervals for the slope coefficients")
# Sensitivity of these tests to the standard-error estimator (HC3, Newey-West) is
# reported once, in the robust-standard-errors cell.
```

```{r coefficient-ci-plot, fig.height=8}
# 90 / 95 / 99% intervals; dashed line = 0 (the null value)
ci_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(term = slopes, level = "90%", low = ci_90[slopes, 1], high = ci_90[slopes, 2]),
  tibble(term = slopes, level = "95%", low = ci_95[slopes, 1], high = ci_95[slopes, 2]),
  tibble(term = slopes, level = "99%", low = ci_99[slopes, 1], high = ci_99[slopes, 2])
) |>
  left_join(select(coef_tests, term, estimate), by = "term") |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = regressors))

ggplot(ci_plot_data, aes(y = level)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high, linewidth = level, colour = level)) +
  geom_point(aes(x = estimate), size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ term, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("90%" = 3, "95%" = 2, "99%" = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("90%" = "steelblue", "95%" = "grey40", "99%" = "grey70"),
                      name = "Confidence level") +
  labs(title = "Coefficient estimates with confidence intervals",
       x = "Coefficient (point = OLS estimate)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r joint-tests}
# Joint F-tests (Wald) on groups of slopes of model_initial.
# H0: every coefficient in the group is 0; H1: at least one is non-zero.
# Classical F-test, plus robust versions using HC3 and Newey-West covariances.
joint_groups <- list(
  "All slopes (overall significance)" = regressors,
  "Global factors: SP500, WTI, VIX" = c("SP500", "WTI", "VIX"),
  "Domestic macro: PH_CPI, PH_M3, PH_Manufacturing_Production" =
    c("PH_CPI", "PH_M3", "PH_Manufacturing_Production"),
  "Monetary and FX: BSP_RRP_Rate, PH_10Y_GS_Yield, USD_PHP" =
    c("BSP_RRP_Rate", "PH_10Y_GS_Yield", "USD_PHP"),
  "Individually significant three: USD_PHP, PH_10Y_GS_Yield, WTI" =
    c("USD_PHP", "PH_10Y_GS_Yield", "WTI")
)
# (the redundancy test for the six insignificant regressors is the M1 vs M4 pair in
# the anova-f-test and wald-test cells)

joint_test <- function(group, vcov. = NULL) {
  hyp <- paste0(group, " = 0")
  res <- if (is.null(vcov.)) linearHypothesis(model_initial, hyp, test = "F")
         else linearHypothesis(model_initial, hyp, vcov. = vcov., test = "F")
  tibble(F = res$F[2], p = res[["Pr(>F)"]][2])
}

imap(joint_groups, function(group, name) {
  cls   <- joint_test(group)
  rob3  <- joint_test(group, hc3(model_initial))
  robnw <- joint_test(group, nw(model_initial))
  tibble(
    test_group       = name,
    H0               = paste0("b = 0 for all ", length(group), " coefficients"),
    q                = length(group),
    df_resid         = df_res,
    F_classical      = signif(cls$F, 4),
    p_classical      = fmt_p(cls$p),
    p_hc3            = fmt_p(rob3$p),
    p_newey_west     = fmt_p(robnw$p),
    decision_classical = if_else(cls$p < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0")
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint F-tests on groups of coefficients (alpha = 0.05)")
```

```{r model-fit}
# Candidate models, all estimated on the same complete-case sample (n = 95)
regs_core     <- c("USD_PHP", "PH_10Y_GS_Yield", "WTI")
regs_domestic <- c("BSP_RRP_Rate", "PH_CPI", "PH_M3", "PH_Manufacturing_Production")
regs_market   <- c("USD_PHP", "PH_10Y_GS_Yield", "WTI", "SP500", "VIX")

candidate_models <- list(
  "M0: intercept only"             = lm(PSEI ~ 1, data = df_model),
  "M1: core 3 (USD_PHP, 10Y, WTI)" = lm(reformulate(regs_core, "PSEI"), data = df_model),
  "M2: domestic macro 4"           = lm(reformulate(regs_domestic, "PSEI"), data = df_model),
  "M3: market 5"                   = lm(reformulate(regs_market, "PSEI"), data = df_model),
  "M4: full 9"                     = model_initial
)

# In-sample fit. Predicted R-squared uses the leave-one-out PRESS statistic.
tss <- sum((df_model$PSEI - mean(df_model$PSEI))^2)

imap(candidate_models, function(m, name) {
  g     <- glance(m)
  press <- sum((residuals(m) / (1 - hatvalues(m)))^2)
  tibble(
    model               = name,
    n                   = nobs(m),
    n_regressors        = length(coef(m)) - 1,
    r_squared           = g$r.squared,
    adj_r_squared       = g$adj.r.squared,
    predicted_r_squared = 1 - press / tss,
    rmse_in_sample      = sqrt(mean(residuals(m)^2)),
    residual_std_err    = g$sigma,
    f_statistic         = g$statistic,
    f_p_value           = fmt_p(g$p.value)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "In-sample fit of the candidate models")
```

```{r aic-bic}
# Information criteria: lower is better. Delta = difference from the best model.
# AICc corrects AIC for small samples; weights are relative model probabilities.
ic <- imap(candidate_models, function(m, name) {
  k <- attr(logLik(m), "df")   # estimated parameters, incl. the error variance
  tibble(
    model  = name,
    k      = k,
    logLik = as.numeric(logLik(m)),
    AIC    = AIC(m),
    AICc   = AIC(m) + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (nobs(m) - k - 1),
    BIC    = BIC(m)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(
    delta_AIC   = AIC  - min(AIC),
    delta_AICc  = AICc - min(AICc),
    delta_BIC   = BIC  - min(BIC),
    weight_AICc = exp(-0.5 * delta_AICc) / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_AICc)),
    weight_BIC  = exp(-0.5 * delta_BIC)  / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_BIC)),
    rank_AIC    = rank(AIC),
    rank_BIC    = rank(BIC)
  )

ic |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "AIC, AICc and BIC (lower is better)")

tibble(
  criterion = c("AIC", "AICc", "BIC"),
  preferred = c(ic$model[which.min(ic$AIC)], ic$model[which.min(ic$AICc)],
                ic$model[which.min(ic$BIC)])
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model preferred by each criterion")
```

```{r anova-f-test}
# Nested-model F-tests. H0: the extra coefficients in the larger model are all 0.
# Pairs are (restricted, full) positions in candidate_models.
nested_pairs <- list(c(1, 5), c(2, 5), c(3, 5), c(4, 5), c(2, 4))

map(nested_pairs, function(p) {
  r <- candidate_models[[p[1]]]
  f <- candidate_models[[p[2]]]
  a <- anova(r, f)
  tibble(
    restricted     = names(candidate_models)[p[1]],
    full           = names(candidate_models)[p[2]],
    extra_terms    = paste(setdiff(names(coef(f)), names(coef(r))), collapse = ", "),
    q              = abs(a$Df[2]),
    df_resid       = a$Res.Df[2],
    RSS_restricted = a$RSS[1],
    RSS_full       = a$RSS[2],
    F              = a$F[2],
    p_value        = fmt_p(a[["Pr(>F)"]][2]),
    decision       = if_else(a[["Pr(>F)"]][2] < 0.05, "Reject H0 (keep extra terms)",
                             "Fail to reject H0 (restriction holds)")
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Nested-model F-tests (alpha = 0.05)")
```

```{r wald-test}
# Wald tests of the same nested restrictions. Classical Wald uses the usual
# covariance matrix; HC3 and Newey-West give versions robust to heteroskedasticity
# and autocorrelation. Chi-square and F versions are both reported.
wald_row <- function(r, f, vcov. = NULL) {
  args_F <- list(r, f, test = "F")
  args_C <- list(r, f, test = "Chisq")
  if (!is.null(vcov.)) { args_F$vcov <- vcov.; args_C$vcov <- vcov. }
  wF <- do.call(waldtest, args_F)
  wC <- do.call(waldtest, args_C)
  tibble(F = wF$F[2], p_F = wF[["Pr(>F)"]][2],
         chisq = wC$Chisq[2], p_chisq = wC[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2])
}

map(nested_pairs, function(p) {
  r <- candidate_models[[p[1]]]
  f <- candidate_models[[p[2]]]
  cls   <- wald_row(r, f)
  rob3  <- wald_row(r, f, hc3)
  robnw <- wald_row(r, f, nw)
  tibble(
    restricted        = names(candidate_models)[p[1]],
    full              = names(candidate_models)[p[2]],
    q                 = abs(length(coef(f)) - length(coef(r))),
    chisq_classical   = cls$chisq, p_chisq_classical = fmt_p(cls$p_chisq),
    F_classical       = cls$F,     p_F_classical     = fmt_p(cls$p_F),
    F_hc3             = rob3$F,    p_F_hc3           = fmt_p(rob3$p_F),
    F_nw              = robnw$F,   p_F_nw            = fmt_p(robnw$p_F)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Wald tests of nested restrictions (classical, HC3 and Newey-West)")
```

```{r stepwise-selection, results='asis'}
# Stepwise selection by AIC (k = 2) and BIC (k = log n). A bidirectional search from
# the full model; forward and backward searches reach the same models here.
upper <- formula(model_initial)

step_specs <- tibble(direction = "both", criterion = c("AIC", "BIC"))

step_models <- pmap(step_specs, function(direction, criterion) {
  step(model_initial,
       scope = list(lower = ~ 1, upper = upper),
       direction = direction,
       k = if (criterion == "AIC") 2 else log(n_obs),
       trace = 0)
})

bind_cols(
  step_specs,
  map(step_models, function(m) tibble(
    selected      = paste(setdiff(names(coef(m)), "(Intercept)"), collapse = ", "),
    n_regressors  = length(coef(m)) - 1,
    adj_r_squared = summary(m)$adj.r.squared,
    AIC           = AIC(m),
    BIC           = BIC(m)
  )) |> bind_rows()
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Stepwise selection results (bidirectional, starting from the full model)")

# selection path for each criterion
for (i in seq_len(nrow(step_specs))) {
  step_models[[i]]$anova |>
    as_tibble() |>
    rename(criterion_value = AIC) |>   # holds AIC or BIC depending on k
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Selection path: both directions, ",
                                  step_specs$criterion[i])) |>
    print()
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

```{r diagnostics-setup}
# Diagnostics for model_initial (full 9-regressor OLS). Data used in the fit, with
# the month of each observation, so residual-based results can be traced to dates.
diag_resid <- residuals(model_initial)

# a plain data frame whose row names match the model's, which lmtest::bptest needs to
# align auxiliary-regression data with the model frame
df_diag <- as.data.frame(df_model)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(df_diag), names(diag_resid)))

diag_fit   <- fitted(model_initial)
diag_n     <- nobs(model_initial)
diag_k     <- length(coef(model_initial))     # parameters, incl. intercept

# one-row summary of an htest object
htest_row <- function(label, h) tibble(
  test      = label,
  statistic = unname(h$statistic),
  df        = paste(h$parameter, collapse = ", "),
  p_value   = fmt_p(h$p.value),
  decision  = if_else(h$p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0")
)
```

```{r heteroskedasticity, fig.height=4}
# H0: errors are homoskedastic; H1: the error variance depends on the regressors
# (or on the fitted values for the White-type test). Rejecting H0 means classical
# standard errors are unreliable.
white_vars <- reformulate(c(
  paste0("(", paste(regressors, collapse = " + "), ")^2"),
  paste0("I(", regressors, "^2)")
))

df_het <- mutate(df_diag, fit = diag_fit)

bind_rows(
  htest_row("Breusch-Pagan (studentized / Koenker)", bptest(model_initial, studentize = TRUE)),
  htest_row("Breusch-Pagan (non-studentized)",       bptest(model_initial, studentize = FALSE)),
  htest_row("White-type (fitted, fitted^2)",
            bptest(model_initial, ~ fit + I(fit^2), data = df_het)),
  htest_row("White (regressors, squares, cross-products)",
            bptest(model_initial, white_vars, data = df_diag))
) |>
  mutate(statistic = signif(statistic, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Heteroskedasticity tests (H0: homoskedastic errors)")

# residuals vs fitted values, and scale-location (spread of residuals vs fitted)
het_data <- tibble(fitted = diag_fit, resid = diag_resid,
                   sqrt_abs_std = sqrt(abs(rstandard(model_initial))))

ggplot(het_data, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "steelblue", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs fitted values", x = "Fitted PSEI return", y = "Residual") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(het_data, aes(fitted, sqrt_abs_std)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "steelblue", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(title = "Scale-location", x = "Fitted PSEI return",
       y = "sqrt(|standardised residual|)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r autocorrelation, fig.height=4}
# H0: no serial correlation in the errors; H1: first-order (DW) or up-to-order-p
# (Breusch-Godfrey) autocorrelation. Rows are in month order.
dw_value <- unname(dwtest(model_initial)$statistic)

bind_rows(
  htest_row("Durbin-Watson (H1: positive autocorrelation)", dwtest(model_initial, alternative = "greater")),
  htest_row("Durbin-Watson (H1: two-sided)", dwtest(model_initial, alternative = "two.sided")),
  htest_row("Breusch-Godfrey, order 1",  bgtest(model_initial, order = 1)),
  htest_row("Breusch-Godfrey, order 3",  bgtest(model_initial, order = 3)),
  htest_row("Breusch-Godfrey, order 6",  bgtest(model_initial, order = 6)),
  htest_row("Breusch-Godfrey, order 12", bgtest(model_initial, order = 12)),
  htest_row("Ljung-Box, 6 lags (residuals)",  Box.test(diag_resid, lag = 6,  type = "Ljung-Box")),
  htest_row("Ljung-Box, 12 lags (residuals)", Box.test(diag_resid, lag = 12, type = "Ljung-Box"))
) |>
  mutate(statistic = signif(statistic, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Autocorrelation tests (H0: no serial correlation). ",
                                "DW = ", round(dw_value, 3),
                                "; implied lag-1 correlation about ", round(1 - dw_value / 2, 3)))

# residuals over time, and residual autocorrelation function
tibble(year_month = df_diag$year_month, resid = diag_resid) |>
  ggplot(aes(year_month, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Residuals over time", x = NULL, y = "Residual") +

acf_res <- acf(diag_resid, lag.max = 24, plot = FALSE)
tibble(lag = as.numeric(acf_res$lag)[-1], acf = as.numeric(acf_res$acf)[-1]) |>
  ggplot(aes(lag, acf)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) / sqrt(diag_n),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(title = "Residual ACF", subtitle = "dashed lines: 95% bounds under no autocorrelation",
       x = "Lag (months)", y = "Autocorrelation") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r normality, fig.height=4}
# H0: residuals are normally distributed. Normality matters for exact t/F inference
# in small samples (n = 95); with large n, OLS inference is asymptotically valid.
res_skew   <- skewness(diag_resid)
res_exkurt <- excess_kurtosis(diag_resid)

# Jarque-Bera: JB = n/6 * (S^2 + (excess K)^2 / 4) ~ chi-square(2) under H0
jb_stat <- diag_n / 6 * (res_skew^2 + res_exkurt^2 / 4)
jb_test <- list(statistic = c(JB = jb_stat), parameter = c(df = 2),
                p.value = pchisq(jb_stat, df = 2, lower.tail = FALSE))

bind_rows(
  htest_row("Shapiro-Wilk", shapiro.test(diag_resid)),
  htest_row("Jarque-Bera",  jb_test)
) |>
  mutate(statistic = signif(statistic, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(
    "Normality tests on residuals (skewness = %.3f, excess kurtosis = %.3f)",
    res_skew, res_exkurt))

# Q-Q plot and residual histogram with a normal curve
ggplot(tibble(resid = diag_resid), aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_qq_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Normal Q-Q plot of residuals",
       x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(tibble(resid = diag_resid), aes(resid)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mean(diag_resid), sd = sd(diag_resid)),
                colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residual distribution vs normal", x = "Residual", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r specification-reset}
  htest_row("RESET: squares of regressors", resettest(model_initial, power = 2, type = "regressor"))
```

```{r multicollinearity-vif, fig.height=4}
# VIF_j = 1 / (1 - R2_j), where R2_j is from regressing X_j on the other regressors.
# Rules of thumb: >= 5 moderate, >= 10 severe collinearity.
vif_values <- car::vif(model_initial)

vif_table <- tibble(
  variable  = names(vif_values),
  VIF       = as.numeric(vif_values),
  tolerance = 1 / VIF,
  R2_on_others = 1 - tolerance,
  flag      = case_when(VIF >= 10 ~ "severe (>= 10)", VIF >= 5 ~ "moderate (>= 5)",
                        TRUE ~ "low (< 5)")
) |>
  arrange(desc(VIF))

vif_table |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf("Variance inflation factors (mean VIF = %.3f)", mean(vif_values)))

# condition number of the standardised design matrix (> 30 suggests collinearity)
x_std <- scale(model.matrix(model_initial)[, -1])
sv    <- svd(x_std)$d
tibble(statistic = c("Largest / smallest singular value (condition number)"),
       value = round(max(sv) / min(sv), 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Condition number of the standardised regressors")

ggplot(vif_table, aes(VIF, reorder(variable, VIF))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 10), linetype = "dashed", colour = c("orange", "firebrick")) +
  labs(title = "Variance inflation factors",
       subtitle = "dashed lines: 5 (moderate) and 10 (severe)", x = "VIF", y = NULL) +
```

```{r influence-diagnostics, fig.height=4}
# Influence: Cook's distance, leverage (hat values), studentised residuals, DFFITS
# and DFBETAS. Common cut-offs: Cook's D > 4/n, leverage > 2k/n, |rstudent| > 2,
# |DFFITS| > 2*sqrt(k/n), |DFBETAS| > 2/sqrt(n).
cut_cook <- 4 / diag_n
cut_hat  <- 2 * diag_k / diag_n
cut_rstu <- 2
cut_dffits <- 2 * sqrt(diag_k / diag_n)
cut_dfb  <- 2 / sqrt(diag_n)

dfb_mat <- dfbetas(model_initial)

infl_table <- tibble(
  year_month = df_diag$year_month,
  cooks_d    = cooks.distance(model_initial),
  leverage   = hatvalues(model_initial),
  rstudent   = rstudent(model_initial),
  dffits     = dffits(model_initial),
  n_dfbetas_flagged = rowSums(abs(dfb_mat) > cut_dfb)
) |>
  mutate(
    flag_cook = cooks_d > cut_cook,
    flag_hat  = leverage > cut_hat,
    flag_rstu = abs(rstudent) > cut_rstu,
    flag_dffits = abs(dffits) > cut_dffits,
    n_flags   = flag_cook + flag_hat + flag_rstu + flag_dffits
  )

tibble(
  measure = c("Cook's distance", "Leverage", "|Studentised residual|", "|DFFITS|",
              "Any |DFBETAS|"),
  cutoff  = c(cut_cook, cut_hat, cut_rstu, cut_dffits, cut_dfb),
  n_flagged = c(sum(infl_table$flag_cook), sum(infl_table$flag_hat),
                sum(infl_table$flag_rstu), sum(infl_table$flag_dffits),
                sum(infl_table$n_dfbetas_flagged > 0)),
  max_value = c(max(infl_table$cooks_d), max(infl_table$leverage),
                max(abs(infl_table$rstudent)), max(abs(infl_table$dffits)),
                max(abs(dfb_mat)))
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Influence measures: cut-offs and number of flagged months")

infl_table |>
  arrange(desc(cooks_d)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ten most influential months (by Cook's distance)")

# Cook's distance over time
ggplot(infl_table, aes(year_month, cooks_d)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = flag_cook), width = 25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cut_cook, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Cook's distance by month", subtitle = "dashed line: 4/n",
       x = NULL, y = "Cook's D") +
  theme_minimal()


# leverage vs studentised residual (point size = Cook's D); flagged months labelled
ggplot(infl_table, aes(leverage, rstudent)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-cut_rstu, cut_rstu), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cut_hat, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = cooks_d, colour = n_flags > 0), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = filter(infl_table, n_flags >= 2),
            aes(label = format(year_month, "%b %Y")), size = 3, vjust = -1,
            check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey50", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
                      name = "Flagged by any measure") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Cook's D") +
  labs(title = "Leverage vs studentised residual",
       subtitle = "dashed lines: 2k/n (leverage) and +/-2 (studentised residual)",
       x = "Leverage (hat value)", y = "Studentised residual") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r stability-cusum-chow, fig.height=4.5}
# Parameter stability. H0: coefficients are constant over the sample.
# CUSUM tests detect gradual drift; Chow tests a break at a known date; the sup-F
# (Andrews) test searches for an unknown break date.
cusum_ols <- efp(mlr_formula, data = df_diag, type = "OLS-CUSUM")
cusum_rec <- efp(mlr_formula, data = df_diag, type = "Rec-CUSUM")

# Chow tests: the first segment ends at the given month
break_dates <- as.Date(c("2020-03-01", "2021-12-01", "2022-04-01"))
break_labels <- c("after Mar 2020 (COVID-19 shock)",
                  "after Dec 2021 (sample midpoint)",
                  "after Apr 2022 (start of BSP tightening)")
break_idx <- map_int(break_dates, ~ which(df_diag$year_month == .x))

chow_rows <- map2(break_idx, break_labels, function(idx, label) {
  htest_row(paste0("Chow: ", label),
            sctest(mlr_formula, data = df_diag, type = "Chow", point = idx))
})

fs <- Fstats(mlr_formula, data = df_diag, from = 0.15)
supf <- sctest(fs, type = "supF")
supf_idx <- breakpoints(fs)$breakpoints

bind_rows(
  htest_row("OLS-CUSUM", sctest(cusum_ols)),
  htest_row("Recursive CUSUM", sctest(cusum_rec)),
  chow_rows,
  htest_row("sup-F (unknown break date)", supf)
) |>
  mutate(statistic = signif(statistic, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Stability tests (H0: stable coefficients)")

tibble(
  statistic = "Most likely break date from the sup-F search",
  value = format(df_diag$year_month[supf_idx], "%Y-%m")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Estimated break (first segment ends in this month)")

plot(cusum_ols, main = "OLS-CUSUM test of parameter stability")
plot(cusum_rec, main = "Recursive CUSUM test of parameter stability")
plot(fs, main = "F statistics for a break at each candidate date")
```

```{r robust-standard-errors, fig.height=8}
# Robustness of inference to the standard-error estimator. HC3 corrects for
# heteroskedasticity; Newey-West (HAC) also allows autocorrelation.
nw_lag_auto <- bwNeweyWest(model_initial, prewhite = FALSE)

vcov_list <- list(
  Classical            = vcov(model_initial),
  HC3                  = hc3(model_initial),
  `Newey-West (auto)`  = nw(model_initial),
  `Newey-West (lag 6)` = nw(model_initial, lag = 6)
)

robust_results <- imap(vcov_list, function(V, method) {
  ct <- coeftest(model_initial, vcov. = V)
  ci <- coefci(model_initial, vcov. = V, level = 0.95)
  tibble(
    method   = method,
    term     = rownames(ct),
    estimate = ct[, 1],
    std_error = ct[, 2],
    t_stat   = ct[, 3],
    p_value  = ct[, 4],
    ci_lower = ci[, 1],
    ci_upper = ci[, 2]
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = names(vcov_list)))

# standard errors and p-values side by side
robust_results |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  select(term, method, std_error, p_value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = c(std_error, p_value),
              names_glue = "{.value} {method}") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(
    "Standard errors and p-values by estimator (Newey-West automatic bandwidth = %.2f)",
    nw_lag_auto))

# significance decisions and inflation of standard errors relative to classical
robust_results |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  group_by(term) |>
  summarise(
    `SE ratio HC3 / classical`        = std_error[method == "HC3"] / std_error[method == "Classical"],
    `SE ratio NW (auto) / classical`  = std_error[method == "Newey-West (auto)"] / std_error[method == "Classical"],
    sig_classical = p_value[method == "Classical"] < alpha,
    sig_hc3       = p_value[method == "HC3"] < alpha,
    sig_nw_auto   = p_value[method == "Newey-West (auto)"] < alpha,
    sig_nw_lag6   = p_value[method == "Newey-West (lag 6)"] < alpha,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Does the significance decision (5%) change with the estimator?")

# overall significance with robust covariance matrices
map(vcov_list, function(V) {
  w <- linearHypothesis(model_initial, paste0(regressors, " = 0"), vcov. = V, test = "F")
  tibble(F = w$F[2], p_value = fmt_p(w[["Pr(>F)"]][2]))
}) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "method") |>
  mutate(F = signif(F, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Overall F-test (H0: all slopes = 0) by covariance estimator")

# 95% confidence intervals by estimator
robust_results |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = regressors)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = method, colour = method)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = estimate), size = 2, colour = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ term, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "95% confidence intervals by standard-error estimator",
       x = "Coefficient", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r remedy-setup}
# Data and helpers for the corrective steps. Everything is estimated on the same
# months and the same dependent variable (PSEI), so the models are comparable.
df_rem <- df_diag |>
  mutate(MARCH_2020 = as.integer(year_month == as.Date("2020-03-01")))

# Coefficient table with classical and HC3 inference. A single-month dummy gives that
# month leverage 1, which makes HC3 undefined; for such models (dummy = its name) the
# HC3 results for the other coefficients come from the fit without that month, which
# has identical coefficients, and the dummy keeps its classical standard error.
inference_table <- function(m, dummy = NULL) {
  ct_c <- coeftest(m)
  if (is.null(dummy)) {
    m_h <- m
  } else {
    m_h <- lm(update(formula(m), paste(". ~ . -", dummy)), data = df_rem[df_rem[[dummy]] == 0, ])
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(coef(m_h)), unname(coef(m)[names(coef(m_h))]))))
  }
  ct_h <- coeftest(m_h, vcov. = hc3(m_h))
  ci_h <- coefci(m_h, vcov. = hc3(m_h), level = 0.95)
  out <- tibble(
    term         = rownames(ct_h),
    estimate     = ct_h[, 1],
    se_classical = ct_c[rownames(ct_h), 2],
    se_hc3       = ct_h[, 2],
    t_hc3        = ct_h[, 3],
    p_classical  = ct_c[rownames(ct_h), 4],
    p_hc3        = ct_h[, 4],
    ci95_low     = ci_h[, 1],
    ci95_high    = ci_h[, 2]
  )
  if (!is.null(dummy)) {
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(term = dummy, estimate = ct_c[dummy, 1],
                                 se_classical = ct_c[dummy, 2], p_classical = ct_c[dummy, 4]))
  }
  out
}

# one-row summary of fit and diagnostics for a model
diag_summary <- function(m, label) {
  e  <- residuals(m)
  n  <- length(e)
  cd <- cooks.distance(m)
  tibble(
    model           = label,
    n               = n,
    n_regressors    = length(coef(m)) - 1,
    adj_r_squared   = summary(m)$adj.r.squared,
    AIC             = AIC(m),
    BIC             = BIC(m),
    bp_p            = bptest(m)$p.value,
    reset_p         = resettest(m, power = 2:3, type = "fitted")$p.value,
    shapiro_p       = shapiro.test(e)$p.value,
    dw_p            = dwtest(m, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
    # an observation with leverage 1 (a single-month dummy) has an undefined Cook's D
    max_cooks_d     = max(cd, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cooks_flagged = sum(cd > 4 / n, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}
```

```{r remedy-1-hc3}
# STEP 1: robust standard errors. The OLS estimates stay the same; inference uses
# HC3, which is valid under heteroskedasticity of unknown form and performs better
# than HC0-HC2 at n = 95. Residuals show no autocorrelation, so HAC is not needed.
# (Estimator comparison and the overall F-test: see robust-standard-errors above.)
tab_init <- inference_table(model_initial)

tab_init |>
  mutate(
    se_ratio = se_hc3 / se_classical,
    decision_changes = (p_classical < alpha) != (p_hc3 < alpha),
    across(c(p_classical, p_hc3), fmt_p)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  select(term, estimate, se_classical, se_hc3, se_ratio, t_hc3, p_classical, p_hc3,
         ci95_low, ci95_high, decision_changes) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Step 1: initial model with HC3 standard errors (95% CIs use HC3)")
```

```{r remedy-2-march-dummy, fig.height=4}
# STEP 2: a dummy for March 2020, the dominant influential observation (Cook's D,
# leverage, DFBETAS for WTI and VIX). It is a real, identifiable event, so it is
# modelled rather than deleted. A single-month dummy fits that month exactly, which
# makes the other coefficients identical to an OLS fit that omits March 2020, but the
# month stays in the sample and its effect is estimated.
model_march <- lm(update(mlr_formula, . ~ . + MARCH_2020), data = df_rem)
tab_march   <- inference_table(model_march, dummy = "MARCH_2020")

tab_march |>
  mutate(across(c(p_classical, p_hc3), fmt_p)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Step 2: model with a March 2020 dummy (HC3 from the 94-month fit; the dummy row uses its classical SE)")

tab_init |>
  select(term, est_initial = estimate, p_initial = p_hc3) |>
  inner_join(select(tab_march, term, est_march = estimate, p_march = p_hc3), by = "term") |>
  mutate(
    pct_change = 100 * (est_march - est_initial) / abs(est_initial),
    sig_initial = p_initial < alpha,
    sig_march   = p_march < alpha,
    across(c(p_initial, p_march), fmt_p)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Effect of the March 2020 dummy on the estimates (significance by HC3 p-values)")

a <- anova(model_initial, model_march)
tibble(test = "Nested F-test: add MARCH_2020 (H0: coefficient = 0)",
       F = signif(a$F[2], 4), p_value = fmt_p(a[["Pr(>F)"]][2])) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Is the March 2020 dummy significant?")

# influence before and after
cd_march <- cooks.distance(model_march)
infl_compare <- bind_rows(
  tibble(model = "Initial", year_month = df_rem$year_month,
         cooks_d = cooks.distance(model_initial)),
  tibble(model = "March 2020 dummy", year_month = df_rem$year_month,
         cooks_d = if_else(is.nan(cd_march), 0, cd_march))
)

ggplot(infl_compare, aes(year_month, cooks_d)) +
  geom_col(width = 25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4 / nrow(df_rem), linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Cook's distance by month", subtitle = "dashed line: 4/n",
       x = NULL, y = "Cook's D") +
  theme_minimal()

tibble(year_month = df_rem$year_month, cooks_d = cd_march) |>
  filter(!is.nan(cooks_d)) |>
  arrange(desc(cooks_d)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(cooks_d = signif(cooks_d, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Most influential months after the March 2020 dummy")
```

```{r remedy-3-robust-regression}
# STEP 3: robust (M-estimation) regression. Huber and MM estimators downweight
# observations with large residuals instead of deleting them or modelling them with
# dummies. MM also resists high-leverage points. Weights show which months are
# treated as outliers. Standard errors are rlm's asymptotic ones; p-values use a
# t distribution with n - k degrees of freedom (an approximation).
rlm_huber <- MASS::rlm(mlr_formula, data = df_rem, maxit = 100)
set.seed(2026)   # the MM initial estimate uses random subsampling
rlm_mm    <- MASS::rlm(mlr_formula, data = df_rem, method = "MM", maxit = 100)

rlm_inference <- function(m) {
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  dfres <- nrow(df_rem) - nrow(cf)
  tibble(
    term     = rownames(cf),
    estimate = cf[, "Value"],
    se       = cf[, "Std. Error"],
    t        = cf[, "t value"],
    p        = 2 * pt(-abs(cf[, "t value"]), dfres),
    ci95_low = estimate - qt(0.975, dfres) * se,
    ci95_high = estimate + qt(0.975, dfres) * se
  )
}

tab_huber <- rlm_inference(rlm_huber)
tab_mm    <- rlm_inference(rlm_mm)

tab_init |>
  select(term, OLS = estimate, p_OLS_hc3 = p_hc3) |>
  left_join(select(tab_huber, term, Huber = estimate, p_Huber = p), by = "term") |>
  left_join(select(tab_mm,    term, MM = estimate,    p_MM = p),    by = "term") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("p_"), fmt_p)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Step 3: OLS vs robust regression (OLS p-values use HC3)")

tibble(
  estimator = c("OLS", "Huber", "MM"),
  residual_scale = c(sigma(model_initial), rlm_huber$s, rlm_mm$s)
) |>
  mutate(residual_scale = signif(residual_scale, 4)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Residual scale: robust fits are less inflated by outliers")

# which months are downweighted
tibble(year_month = df_rem$year_month,
       residual_ols = residuals(model_initial),
       weight_huber = rlm_huber$w,
       weight_mm    = rlm_mm$w) |>
  arrange(weight_mm) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ten most downweighted months (weight 1 = full weight)")
```

```{r remedy-4-reduced-model}
# STEP 4: reduced model as a comparison (variable selection, not a fix for a
# diagnostic problem). BIC and the nested F-tests favoured USD_PHP, PH_10Y_GS_Yield

model_reduced <- lm(reformulate(c(regs_core, "MARCH_2020"), "PSEI"), data = df_rem)

# nested test against the model with all regressors plus the dummy

tibble(test = "Nested F-test: drop the six insignificant regressors (H0: all zero)",
```

```{r remedy-comparison, fig.height=9}
# Compare the initial model with every remedy: fit, information criteria,
# diagnostics, cross-validated error, and coefficients. Cross-validation uses 10
# random folds (time order is ignored); March 2020 errors are reported separately
# because a held-out dummy month cannot be predicted by its own dummy. The robust
# fits are compared on cross-validated error only: their weighted likelihood,
# R-squared and residual tests are not comparable with the OLS ones.
set.seed(2026)
foldid <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(df_rem)))

# out-of-fold prediction errors, pooled over all months
oof_errors <- function(fit_fun, data = df_rem) {
  err <- numeric(nrow(data))
  for (k in 1:10) {
    train <- data[foldid != k, ]
    test  <- data[foldid == k, ]
    err[foldid == k] <- test$PSEI - suppressWarnings(predict(fit_fun(train), newdata = test))
  }
  err
}

ols_models <- list(
  "Initial (OLS)"            = model_initial,
  "March 2020 dummy"         = model_march,
  "Reduced (core 3 + dummy)" = model_reduced
)

fit_funs <- list(
  "Initial (OLS)"            = function(d) lm(mlr_formula, data = d),
  "March 2020 dummy"         = function(d) lm(formula(model_march), data = d),
  "Robust: Huber"            = function(d) MASS::rlm(mlr_formula, data = d, maxit = 100),
  "Robust: MM"               = function(d) MASS::rlm(mlr_formula, data = d, method = "MM", maxit = 100),
  "Reduced (core 3 + dummy)" = function(d) lm(formula(model_reduced), data = d)
)

mar_idx <- which(df_rem$year_month == as.Date("2020-03-01"))
cv_table <- imap(fit_funs, function(f, label) {
  e <- oof_errors(f, data = df_rem)
  tibble(model = label, cv_rmse_all = sqrt(mean(e^2)),
         cv_rmse_excl_mar2020 = sqrt(mean(e[-mar_idx]^2)))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

ols_summary <- imap(ols_models, ~ diag_summary(.x, .y)) |> bind_rows()

cv_table |>
  left_join(select(ols_summary, model, n_regressors, adj_r_squared, AIC, BIC), by = "model") |>
  select(model, n_regressors, adj_r_squared, AIC, BIC, cv_rmse_all, cv_rmse_excl_mar2020) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fit and 10-fold cross-validated RMSE (robust fits: cross-validated error only)")

ols_summary |>
  select(model, bp_p, reset_p, shapiro_p, dw_p, max_cooks_d, n_cooks_flagged) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Diagnostics re-run on each OLS model (Breusch-Pagan, RESET, Shapiro-Wilk, Durbin-Watson p-values)")

# coefficients side by side: OLS rows use HC3 p-values, robust rows rlm's p-values
coef_sources <- list(
  "Initial (OLS)"            = tab_init |> transmute(term, estimate, p = coalesce(p_hc3, p_classical)),
  "March 2020 dummy"         = tab_march |> transmute(term, estimate, p = coalesce(p_hc3, p_classical)),
  "Reduced (core 3 + dummy)" = tab_reduced |> transmute(term, estimate, p = coalesce(p_hc3, p_classical)),
  "Robust: Huber"            = tab_huber |> transmute(term, estimate, p),
  "Robust: MM"               = tab_mm |> transmute(term, estimate, p)
)

imap(coef_sources, function(tab, label) {
  tab |> transmute(term, model = label, cell = sprintf("%.4g (p=%s)", estimate, fmt_p(p)))
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(coef_sources))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Coefficients by model (p-values: HC3 for OLS rows; the March dummy rows use classical)")

# 95% confidence intervals for the nine original regressors
ci_models <- bind_rows(
  tab_init  |> transmute(model = "OLS (HC3)", term, estimate, ci95_low, ci95_high),
  tab_march |> transmute(model = "March 2020 dummy (HC3)", term, estimate, ci95_low, ci95_high),
  tab_huber |> transmute(model = "Huber", term, estimate, ci95_low, ci95_high),
  tab_mm    |> transmute(model = "MM", term, estimate, ci95_low, ci95_high)
) |>
  filter(term %in% regressors) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("OLS (HC3)", "March 2020 dummy (HC3)", "Huber", "MM")),
         term  = factor(term, levels = regressors))

ggplot(ci_models, aes(y = model, colour = model)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = ci95_low, xmax = ci95_high), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = estimate), size = 2, colour = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ term, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "95% confidence intervals: OLS, March 2020 dummy, and robust regression",
       x = "Coefficient", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
